Drawing style: keep exactly the way of drawing of the first two attached reference drawings (bold, even, smooth black ink outlines like an icon coloring page, rich detail, flowing drapery folds, embroidered borders, many small ornaments, thin circular halos), but now fully COLORED with flat, rich, slightly watercolor-like fills inside the black outlines, like an illuminated Coptic icon: warm gold for halos and icon backgrounds, deep ultramarine and crimson for robes and curtains, white and cream vestments with red and gold crosses, dark ebony and warm brown wood with pale ivory and mother-of-pearl geometric inlay, cream limestone walls, terracotta and warm stone floors, soft gold accents on lamps, candlesticks, crosses and the ciborium. Keep the black outlines strong and clear everywhere. IMPORTANT: every human and angelic face is left completely blank, a smooth empty oval in a light skin tone with no eyes, no eyebrows, no nose and no mouth; hair, beards, ears, hands, halos and clothes are drawn and colored in full detail. No text, no letters (except the simple Greek letters Alpha and Omega where requested), no frame, no border, no signature. Accurate to a real Coptic Orthodox church in Egypt: no pews unless stated, no Western or Byzantine styling, no statues. All clergy and deacons are barefoot at the altar.
Scene: The khorus (the raised choir area between the nave and the haikal screen) of a Coptic Orthodox church during the Liturgy of the Word, drawn accurately. The haikal screen of dark wood with ivory inlay and its curtained doors forms the back wall, with hanging lamps and a star-patterned vault. The khorus is raised on three steps, with a carved wooden railing in front. A deacon reads the Gospel from a tall wooden lectern (manara) with an open Gospel book; deacons in white tunics with crossing stoles stand in two groups on both sides playing brass cymbals and a triangle (the only instruments of the Coptic Church), others chant holding hymn books; two seven-branch candelabra with burning candles. In front of the railing the congregation STANDS on the stone floor, men on the left and veiled women on the right with children, with a clear central aisle; there are NO pews. Warm lamp light, cream walls, columns with carved capitals topped with crosses.
